TCP long-lived connections: attention (WARN)
Node: 192.0.2.10:9000 · IPv4 · TCP
Method version: 1
Elapsed: 10 min
Parameters
  Dial timeout: 1 s
  Test duration: 10 min
  Heartbeat interval: 30 s
  Heartbeat reply timeout: 1 s
  Maximum reconnect wait: 1 s
  Minimum reconnect wait: 100 ms
  New connections per second, max: 1
  Target connections: 50
  TCP keepalive: off
Observed
  Connections made: 73
  Failed dials: 2
  Drops: 31
  Drops (no reply in time): 3
  Drops (closed by peer): 1
  Drops (reset or error): 27
  Drops (wrong reply): 0
  Heartbeats sent: 233
  Heartbeats acknowledged: 200
  Heartbeats acknowledged after a full idle interval: 120
  Echo round trip p50: 211 µs (40 samples)
  Echo round trip p95: 309 µs (40 samples)
  Echo round trip p99: too few samples (40)
  Mean lifetime of dropped connections: 45 s (31 samples)
Inferred
  - Connections that stopped answering without a close or reset: 3. This is the usual sign of a NAT or other middlebox silently dropping connection state.
  - Connections closed by the far side: 1. Either the node ended them (idle timeout or connection limit) or a middlebox sent the close.
  - Connections ended by a reset or another error: 27.
Not proven
  - A node turning connections away at its limit cannot be told apart from the network dropping them; the client sees the same thing.
  - Drops are only noticed at the next heartbeat, so lifetimes are upper bounds, long by up to one heartbeat interval (30 s).
